haiku-low.q1: Split into pages of 500 products by ascending id, using keyset pagination (about 800 pages). Pages are fetched one at a time, never in parallel.
haiku-low.q2: In sync_state as download_last_saved_id. It advances in the same SQLite transaction that saves its page, so only fully saved pages count. Re-fetching a page is harmless under the apply rule.
haiku-low.q3: A watermark is taken before the download. Edits after a page is read arrive via the change feed drain. Edits before are already in the page. Deletes arrive as tombstones, or are missing from the page.
haiku-low.q4: The server returns HTTP 410 resync_required if after_seq is below purged_through_seq. The client keeps the live catalogue, sets resync_pending, and downloads a replacement into the inactive generation.
haiku-low.q5: It is downloaded into the inactive generation, then drained with changes after the watermark. One transaction then sets active_gen to it and live_cursor_seq to the drain position, making it the catalogue reps see.
haiku-low.q6: A trigger: app launch, returning to foreground, or Wi-Fi return (full download only). It runs at most once every 15 minutes, counted from last_incremental_attempt_at, and only when no download is in progress.
haiku-low.q7: It retries the same request up to 5 attempts total, waiting 2, 4, 8 then 16 seconds. After the fifth failure it gives up, keeps saved data, and waits for the next trigger. Status changes depend on the phase.
haiku-low.q8: The page in progress finishes and saves. No further pages are requested, and download_status becomes paused_cellular until Wi-Fi returns and a trigger resumes it. The drain may run on any network.
haiku-low.q9: It writes the row only if its change_seq is greater than or equal to the stored row's change_seq, or if no row is stored. Equal versions are harmlessly rewritten. Incoming deletes remove the row if present.
haiku-low.q10: It starts from live_cursor_seq in sync_state. Each response is applied with next_seq in one transaction, which moves the cursor forward together with the changes it covers.
haiku-low.q11: It reads products' change_seq, returning rows with change_seq greater than n in order, indexed on change_seq. Deletes are soft tombstones with deleted true, kept 7 days, and appear as {id, deleted:true, change_seq}.

sonnet.q1: Keyset pagination ordered by id ascending, 800 pages of 500 products (after_id, limit=500, no offset). Pages are fetched one at a time, never in parallel.
sonnet.q2: In SQLite sync_state.download_last_saved_id. It is updated in the same transaction that saves the page's rows (apply rule), so it advances only when the page is fully saved. On resume it continues from that id, not page 1.
sonnet.q3: Before downloading, POST /sync/begin records a watermark (max committed change_seq). After all pages are saved, the drain replays all changes after the watermark in change_seq order into the download copy using the apply rule. Edits after a page was read arrive via the feed. Edits before are already in the page, and replays are harmless. Deletes arrive as tombstones, or the feed delete does nothing if the row is absent. Edits after the drain's last response are fetched by the first incremental sync, since live_cursor_seq is set to the drain's final position.
sonnet.q4: The changes endpoint answers HTTP 410 {"error":"resync_required"} when after_seq < purged_through_seq. In incremental sync (step 8) the client keeps the live catalogue, sets resync_pending, and starts a full download into the inactive generation (if on Wi-Fi). In a drain (step 9) it discards the partial download and restarts with a fresh watermark from page 1.
sonnet.q5: It is downloaded into the inactive (download) generation table, with pages then the drain applied. The active generation stays untouched and visible meanwhile. It becomes the one the app reads at the swap, a single transaction that sets active_gen = download_gen, live_cursor_seq = download_drain_seq and download_status = none. This happens after the drain finishes (ready_to_swap).
sonnet.q6: Triggers: app launch or the app returning to the foreground (Wi-Fi return is a trigger for full download only). It runs only if no sync pass is running, active_gen is set and download_status is none. At most once every 15 minutes since the last_incremental_attempt_at, which is stored persistently.
sonnet.q7: The wrapper retries: up to 5 attempts in total, waiting 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, then 16 s between attempts, with no wait after the fifth. After the fifth failure it reports gave up. Everything saved stays. During page download status becomes stopped_error. During drain status stays draining. During incremental sync no status changes. The next trigger tries again.
sonnet.q8: The page in progress finishes (including retries) and is saved. Then no more pages are requested and download_status = paused_cellular. On return to Wi-Fi, the trigger resumes it from download_last_saved_id. The drain may run on any network.
sonnet.q9: Apply rule: write the incoming row only if its change_seq is greater than or equal to the stored row's change_seq, or no row is stored. Equal means the same version, so rewriting is harmless. An incoming delete removes the row if present and does nothing if absent.
sonnet.q10: It starts from sync_state.live_cursor_seq (changes?after_seq=live_cursor_seq). It is set to next_seq of each response in the same transaction that applies that response's changes. It is first set at the swap, to download_drain_seq.
sonnet.q11: The feed reads rows with change_seq > after_seq, in change_seq order, from the Catalogue Postgres product table (soft-deleted rows kept as tombstones), using an index on change_seq. Deletes are represented as tombstones {id, deleted:true, change_seq}. Tombstones are kept 7 days, and purged_through_seq is read from a one-row table.
